Content exceeding 10,000 characters is rejected.\n- The server validates all incoming messages against known types. Unrecognized types receive an `INVALID_MESSAGE` error.\n\n## 13. Source Files\n\n| Concern                  | File                                              |\n| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |\n| Shared entry types       | `src/types/session.ts`                            |\n| Backend message types    | `src/types/messages.ts`                           |\n| Backend sender helpers   | `src/transport/ws/sender.ts`                      |\n| Message validation       | `src/transport/ws/validation.ts`                  |\n| Message handling         | `src/transport/ws/messageHandler.ts`              |\n| Connection handler       | `src/transport/ws/connectionHandler.ts`           |\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":345,"oldLines":6,"newStart":345,"newLines":7,"lines":[" - A message the server cannot parse into a known type is answered with `INVALID_MESSAGE`, and no message stream is started for it ([validated by: rejects an unparseable message and never starts a stream](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L74))."," - A rate limit reported by the AI provider is surfaced as `RATE_LIMITED`, which tells the client the same request is worth retrying ([validated by: tells the client to retry when the provider is rate limited](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L337))."," - Any other failure raised while processing a message is reported as `SERVER_ERROR` ([validated by: reports any other failure as a server error](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L346)).","+- A request nothing in the connected deployment can answer — a `list_sessions` against a session store implementing no `listFor` — is answered with `UNSUPPORTED`, telling the client the store cannot list rather than that the user has none ([validated by: answers a store without listFor with UNSUPPORTED rather than an empty list](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L115))."," "," ### 5.7 pong"," "]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_0d776ba2e51f49d18538364f","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

(file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f34bb95e-ddda-48ba-b5d7-5fdeb7a40e4e","uuid":"a716ebde-a51b-4788-8d24-b0ed7c477593","timestamp":"2026-11-06T04:15:15.319Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/bdfb6d0de730/workspace/target/specs/hal-engine-conversation-list/spec.md","oldString":"- A store without `listFor` answers `{type: 'session_list', sessions: []}`, and a throwing `listFor` logs an error on the `ws` category and answers `{type: 'error', code: 'SERVER_ERROR'}` ([validated by: answers an empty session_list when the store has no listFor, and SERVER_ERROR with a ws error log when listFor throws](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L101)).","newString":"- A store without `listFor` is answered on the wire with `{type: 'error', code: 'UNSUPPORTED'}`, never an empty `session_list`, for the same reason a store refuses when its collection cannot list: an empty history is not a safe guess; a throwing `listFor` logs an error on the `ws` category and answers `{type: 'error', code: 'SERVER_ERROR'}` ([validated by: answers UNSUPPORTED when the store has no listFor, and SERVER_ERROR with a ws error log when listFor throws](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L101), [validated by: answers a store without listFor with UNSUPPORTED rather than an empty list](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L115)).","originalFile":"# Conversation List\n\n| Field  | Value                 |\n| ------ | --------------------- |\n| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#143 |\n| Status | Shipped               |\n\nResume gets a client back into one conversation: the id it names, or the user's most recently active one. Neither tells it which conversations exist, and every other member of `SessionStore` answers about a session the caller can already name, so a consumer wanting to offer a conversation list had to query the collection behind the engine's back, against a document shape and a key the engine owns. `listFor` answers the list instead, as summaries rather than sessions. **GDPR.** A summary is personal data — that a user held a conversation, and when — so it carries no conversation content, it is filtered to one user by the query rather than in application code afterwards, and the retention bound stays the consumer's, through the store's `maxAgeMs` and erasure methods and re-cinq/HALEngine#41.\n\n## The summary\n\n- A summary is `sessionId`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt` and `entryCount`, and nothing else: neither the conversation's entries nor its credentials, so a list can never hand over either, even for a session created with credentials ([validated by: carries only its four fields, so a list can never hand over a conversation or a credential](../../src/infrastructure/stores/sessionStoreListSignature.test.ts#L22)).\n- `listFor` is optional, like `latestFor` and `lookup` before it: a store written against the five original members still satisfies the interface, and both shipped stores implement it ([validated by: leaves a store with only the five original members satisfying the interface beside both shipped ones](../../src/infrastructure/stores/sessionStoreListSignature.test.ts#L11)).\n\n## The order a list answers in\n\n- Summaries come back most recent activity first ([validated by: answers newest activity first, headed by the very session latestFor returns](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L27)).\n- The first summary is the session `latestFor` returns, because both read the same activity ([validated by: answers newest activity first, headed by the very session latestFor returns](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L27)).\n- The order is total rather than merely sorted: two conversations last active in the same millisecond are ordered by session id, the larger first, which is what lets a page resume without dropping one of them ([validated by: keeps a conversation tied on activity rather than dropping it across a page boundary](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L141)).\n- In `InMemorySessionStore` that tie-break is the list's alone: `latestFor` breaks the same tie by creation order, so for two tied conversations the head of the list and the session a resume rejoins can differ ([validated by: breaks a tie on activity by session id, where latestFor takes the session created later](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L42)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` answers in order of `updatedAt`, which each `save` moves forward, and its first summary is the session its own `latestFor` returns ([validated by: answers the user's conversations newest saved first, headed by the one latestFor returns](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L31)).\n- It breaks a tie by `_id` in both members, so there the head of the list is the session a resume rejoins even when every conversation shares an `updatedAt` ([validated by: heads the list with the session latestFor returns even when every conversation shares an updatedAt](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L161)).\n\n## What a summary reports\n\n- `InMemorySessionStore` reports the moment `create` was called, the newest entry time as the activity, and the conversation's entry count ([validated by: reports a creation time, the newest activity and the entry count of each conversation](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L53)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` reports the document's `createdAt`, the `updatedAt` its last save wrote, and the counter written beside the entries ([validated by: reports the creation time, the last save and the entry count of each conversation](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L49)).\n- That counter is what a save writes, so a list never reads a conversation to count one ([validated by: counts a conversation from the field a save writes beside the entries](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L95)).\n- A document written before the counter existed reads as a conversation of no entries rather than failing the list, which is what the backlog documented in `docs/session-stores.md` is for ([validated by: reads a conversation saved before the counter existed as one of no entries, rather than failing](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L79)).\n\n## Whose conversations\n\n- A list holds only the asking user's conversations: another user's never appear, and a user with none gets an empty list ([validated by: omits a conversation that aged out and another user's, and answers nothing for a user with none](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L65)).\n- `InMemorySessionStore` omits a conversation that has aged out, as `latestFor` does ([validated by: omits a conversation that aged out and another user's, and answers nothing for a user with none](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L65)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` filters on the user in the database, sorts on `{updatedAt: -1, _id: -1}` — the `{userId: 1, updatedAt: -1}` index `latestFor` already needs serves its leading keys — and asks for a projection that leaves the entries behind ([validated by: asks the database to filter on the user, sort on the index with the id behind it, and never for the entries](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L108)).\n- It answers from that projection alone, so a collection that never returns an entry still lists conversations — the conversation does not leave the database to be listed ([validated by: answers from a projection alone, so a collection that never returns entries still lists conversations](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L181)).\n\n## Paging\n\n- `limit` takes that many of the newest, and `before` resumes after a row, so a client pages by passing back the last summary it saw — `SessionCursor` is `updatedAt` and `sessionId`, which a `SessionSummary` already satisfies ([validated by: pages down the same order: a limit takes the newest, and before takes what is older than it](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L78)).\n- Paging walks every conversation exactly once even when all of them share an activity time, because the cursor carries the session id the order breaks ties on: a tie cannot fall between two pages and be skipped ([validated by: keeps a conversation tied on activity rather than dropping it across a page boundary](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L141)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` pages the same way ([validated by: pages with before and a limit, down the same newest-first order](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L62)).\n- It walks a tie exactly once too, through the same cursor ([validated by: keeps a conversation tied on updatedAt rather than dropping it across a page boundary](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L127)).\n- A list is at most 200 summaries however many are asked for, and 50 when none is asked for, so no caller can ask for an unbounded page ([validated by: answers at most two hundred conversations however many are asked for, and fifty when none is](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L94)).\n- That limit bounds the rows answered, not the rows the database reads to answer them: on `MongoSessionStore` the work is bounded by the `{userId: 1, updatedAt: -1, _id: -1}` index `docs/session-stores.md` prescribes, and under the two-key form Mongo sorts the user's whole history before applying the limit ([validated by: needs the three-key index to answer without sorting the whole history, which the two-key form does not](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L192)).\n- A fractional limit is floored rather than refused, since a slip in a limit is not a reason to deny a user their history ([validated by: floors a fractional limit, and reads a negative or unusable one as none given rather than as nothing](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L104)).\n- A negative limit, and one that is not a usable number, are read as no limit given at all rather than as a limit of none: handing a user an empty history for a typo is the worse reading ([validated by: floors a fractional limit, and reads a negative or unusable one as none given rather than as nothing](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L104)).\n- Only a limit of exactly `0` answers no conversations ([validated by: answers nothing only for a limit of exactly none](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L116)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` answers a limit of `0` without querying, because MongoDB reads `limit: 0` as no limit at all and would otherwise answer with every conversation the filter matches ([validated by: answers a limit of none without asking the database, which reads a limit of zero as no limit at all](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L143)).\n\n## The two shipped stores answer one order\n\n- `InMemorySessionStore` and `MongoSessionStore` list the same conversations in the same order, so a consumer swapping one for the other sees the same conversation list ([validated by: answer the same order for conversations whose activity differs](../../src/infrastructure/stores/storeListAgreement.test.ts#L43)).\n- They break a tie on activity the same way, by session id ([validated by: break a tie on activity the same way, by session id](../../src/infrastructure/stores/storeListAgreement.test.ts#L52)).\n- They page identically through the documented call, `listFor(userId, {limit, before: rows.at(-1)})`, a page at a time until a page comes back empty ([validated by: page the same way through the documented call, two rows at a time from the last row seen](../../src/infrastructure/stores/storeListAgreement.test.ts#L61)).\n\n## A cursor the caller can actually hold\n\n- A cursor's `updatedAt` may be a `Date`, an ISO string or an epoch number, so a summary that went through JSON on its way to a client and back still pages ([validated by: pages on a cursor that has been through JSON, and refuses one carrying no usable moment](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L123)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` reads such a cursor as a date before it queries, since a string compares against no stored BSON date and would quietly match none of them ([validated by: pages on a cursor that has been through JSON, where a string would have matched no stored date](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L150)).\n- A cursor carrying no usable moment is refused with an error naming it, rather than read as no cursor at all, which would answer the first page again and repeat rows a client has already shown ([validated by: pages on a cursor that has been through JSON, and refuses one carrying no usable moment](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L123)).\n\n## A collection that cannot list\n\n- `find` is optional on `CollectionLike`, so an adapter written before conversation lists existed still satisfies the port ([validated by: refuses to list on a collection that implements no find, rather than reporting no conversations](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L175)).\n- A store built on a collection without it refuses to list, rather than reporting that the user has no conversations ([validated by: refuses to list on a collection that implements no find, rather than reporting no conversations](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L175)).\n\n## When the store cannot answer\n\n- A store whose collection fails rejects rather than answering a partial or empty list: what to show a user who may have conversations is the caller's decision, and an empty history is not a safe guess ([validated by: rejects rather than answering a partial list when the collection fails](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L225)).\n\n## Over the WebSocket protocol\n\n- A client sends `{type: 'list_sessions', limit?, before?}` and receives `{type: 'session_list', sessions}` for the socket's authenticated user, with `createdAt` and `updatedAt` serialised as ISO-8601 strings and any client-supplied `userId` ignored ([validated by: answers list_sessions for the authenticated user with ISO dates, forwarding limit and before while ignoring any client userId](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L60), [validated by: answers list_sessions with the socket user's own conversations as ISO dates, however the frame names its user](../../src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts#L94)).\n- A store without `listFor` answers `{type: 'session_list', sessions: []}`, and a throwing `listFor` logs an error on the `ws` category and answers `{type: 'error', code: 'SERVER_ERROR'}` ([validated by: answers an empty session_list when the store has no listFor, and SERVER_ERROR with a ws error log when listFor throws](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L101)).\n- The validator accepts an optional non-negative integer `limit` and an optional `before` cursor whose `sessionId` is 1–128 characters and whose `updatedAt` parses as a valid timestamp, rejecting any other `list_sessions` payload with `INVALID_MESSAGE` without calling `listFor` ([validated by: accepts a bare list_sessions frame and rejects a malformed limit or before with INVALID_MESSAGE without calling listFor](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L130), [validated by: accepts a bare list_sessions frame and one with a limit and cursor, and rejects a malformed limit or before naming the field](../../src/transport/ws/validation.test.ts#L24)).\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":72,"oldLines":5,"newStart":72,"newLines":5,"lines":[" ## Over the WebSocket protocol"," "," - A client sends One built on an injected collection needs that collection to implement `find`: without it,\n`listFor` refuses rather than reporting that the user has no conversations.","newString":"A store you write yourself can leave `listFor` out, in which case it has no conversation list to\noffer, and a client's `list_sessions` frame is answered with an `error` frame (`UNSUPPORTED`) rather\nthan an empty list. One built on an injected collection needs that collection to implement `find`:\nwithout it, `listFor` refuses rather than reporting that the user has no conversations.","originalFile":"# Session stores\n\nA session store decides where a conversation lives and how long it survives. This page exists for\none reason: **which method erases, and which only evicts**, is not guessable from the names, and\ngetting it wrong either destroys a customer's history or fails to honour their erasure request.\n\n## Erases or evicts\n\n| Method | Cache | Durable storage |\n|---|---|---|\n| `delete(sessionId)` | evicts | **erases** — the consumer's erasure primitive; the engine never calls it |\n| `clear()` | evicts everything | untouched |\n| `evict(sessionId)` | evicts | **erases** — the engine's own call, for a session no client received |\n| `eraseConversation(sessionId)` | evicts | **erases that document, permanently** |\n| `eraseOlderThan(cutoff)` | evicts | **erases every document created before `cutoff`** |\n| `eraseAll()` | evicts everything | **erases every document** |\n\n`delete` is the interface's own member and the engine never calls it, so `MongoSessionStore`\nimplements it as a durable deletion — the same thing `eraseConversation` does, reachable by a\nconsumer holding only the `SessionStore` interface. `eraseConversation` is what an erasure request\nunder GDPR Article 17 calls for; `delete` is its synonym.\n\n**`clear` is not.** Its in-memory twin is a harmless cache reset, so a durable `clear` would be an\nunguarded mass erasure reachable by a method name that gives no warning. `eraseAll` is the durable\nwipe, and it says so.\n\n**Read this before wiring `onDisconnect`.** Both `delete` and `evict` erase on this store, so the\none-line migration that restores the pre-0.4 close behaviour —\n`onDisconnect: sessionId => store.delete(sessionId)` — destroys the conversation on every socket\nclose, a blip included. **Point `onDisconnect` at neither.** There is nothing to reclaim by hand:\nthe cache is bounded by `maxAgeMs` and drops stale entries on its own, without touching a\ndocument. A conversation surviving its socket is the feature, not a leak.\n\n## What is never persisted\n\n`MongoSessionStore` strips `authHeaders`, `authorization`, `cookie` and `host` from what it writes,\nat **any depth** — not just the top level, because `ToolEntry.toolInput` carries whatever the model\nproduced and a token can end up nested inside it. The exported `stripCredentialKeys` applies the\nsame rule, so a store you write yourself can make the same guarantee.\n\nOne consequence worth planning for: a conversation reloaded in a fresh process has no\n`authHeaders`, so a tool that reads `ToolContext.authHeaders` sees nothing until the caller\nre-authenticates. That is the correct trade-off — a bearer token stored beside a conversation\noutlives the request it was issued for — and it matches what the transport does on socket close.\n\n## Retention\n\n`eraseOlderThan(cutoff)` is a method you call. The engine ships no scheduler, because a\nlibrary-owned timer keeps your process alive; how often you call it, and what cutoff you pass, is\nthe retention decision, and it belongs to your deployment with a named person behind it.\n\n`InMemorySessionStore`'s `maxAgeMs` is **not** a retention policy. It is a memory bound so the\ndefault store does not grow without limit, and it defaults to eight hours.\n\n## Truth and cache\n\n`MongoSessionStore` keeps an in-process cache because the orchestrator mutates a session in place\nwhile a turn streams, so `get` has to return a stable object. That cache is bounded by `maxAgeMs`\n(eight hours by default, as in `InMemorySessionStore`): a stale entry is dropped on read and swept\nwhen another session is cached, and dropping one erases nothing, because the next `get` reloads it\nfrom the collection. The collection is the truth: a\nsession saved by one store instance is readable by another built on the same collection. The cache\nis not coherent across instances until a `save` — two processes serving the same conversation at\nonce is not something this store supports.\n\n`count()` reports documents, not cache entries, so `delete` does not change it. It counts **every**\nuser's, not one user's: it is an operational figure, and putting it in front of a user would both\nmisreport their history and disclose the size of everyone else's. There is no per-user count — see\n§ Listing a user's conversations for what to do instead.\n\n## Latest session\n\nWith resume's `latest` option on, every connect that names no session id asks `latestFor(userId)`\nfor the user's most recently active conversation. `MongoSessionStore` answers with the user's\ndocument that has the newest `updatedAt`, which each `save` moves forward, so create this index\nwhere the collection lives; the store creates none itself:\n\n<!-- doc-block: none -- a mongo shell command run against the deployment, not code the package ships -->\n```js\ndb.hal_sessions.createIndex({userId: 1, updatedAt: -1, _id: -1});\n```\n\nThe trailing `_id` is there for `listFor`, which sorts on `{updatedAt: -1, _id: -1}`; `latestFor`\nalone would be served by the first two keys. Create the three-key form and both members are served\n— see § Listing a user's conversations for what the two-key form costs.\n\n`InMemorySessionStore` has no `save` to stamp, so it goes by a session's newest entry, or its\ncreation for a session with none, and never returns one that has aged out. A store you write\nyourself can leave `latestFor` out, in which case such a connect simply starts a new session.\n\n## Listing a user's conversations\n\n`listFor(userId, options?)` is optional, and it answers summaries rather than sessions:\n`sessionId`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt` and `entryCount`, most recent activity first. A summary\ncarries no entries and no `authHeaders`, so a conversation list cannot hand over a conversation or\na credential. Its first row is the session `latestFor` returns, because both read the same activity,\nso a list and a resume agree about which conversation is newest.\n\n`options.limit` defaults to 50 and is capped at 200. `options.before` resumes after a row, so a\nclient pages by passing back the last summary it saw — `SessionCursor` is `{updatedAt, sessionId}`,\nwhich a `SessionSummary` already satisfies, so `listFor(userId, {before: rows.at(-1)})` is the whole\nof it. The session id is in the cursor because `updatedAt` alone is not unique: two conversations\nsaved in the same millisecond would straddle a page boundary and one of them would never be listed.\nA `limit` of `0` answers nothing, and a limit that is not a usable number is read as none given.\n\nA store whose database fails rejects rather than answering an empty list: what to show a user who\nmay have conversations is your decision, and \"no conversations\" is not a safe guess.\n\n**Knowing whether another page exists.** `listFor` answers an array and no `hasMore`, so read it off\nthe page: a page shorter than the `limit` you asked for is the last one. A full page is ambiguous, so\neither accept one final round-trip that comes back empty, or ask for one row more than you intend to\nshow — `{limit: pageSize + 1}`, display the first `pageSize`, and take the cursor from the last row\nyou displayed. The extra row's presence is your `hasMore`. Because the limit is capped at 200, that\ntrick works up to a `pageSize` of 199. Do not reach for `count()` for this: it counts every user's\nconversations, not this user's, and there is no per-user total today.\n\n`MongoSessionStore` filters on the user in the query, sorts `{updatedAt: -1, _id: -1}` and projects\nthe entries away, so a page of summaries never carries a conversation out of the database.\n\n**Create the three-key index from § Latest session.** `{userId: 1, updatedAt: -1}` cannot satisfy a\ntwo-key sort, so Mongo answers with a blocking sort over *every* conversation the user has and\napplies the limit after it: measured on 300 conversations, a 50-row page examined all 300 documents,\nwhere the three-key index made the same page an indexed sort examining exactly the 50 it returns. The\nindex does not *cover* the query — `createdAt` and `entryCount` are not in it, so Mongo still fetches\neach row it answers with — and that is the point: with it, the work is the page; without it, the work\nis the history. Two consequences, not just a slow query — paging a long history that way is\nquadratic, and a blocking sort is bounded by Mongo's 100 MB sort limit, so a large enough history\nmakes `listFor` fail rather than merely crawl.\n\nIt answers a `limit` of `0` without querying at all, because MongoDB reads `limit: 0` as *no* limit\nand would otherwise hand back everything the filter matches. It counts a conversation from an\n`entryCount` field each `save` writes beside the entries. A document saved before 0.6 has no such\nfield and lists as a conversation of no entries until you backfill it:\n\n<!-- doc-block: none -- a mongo shell command run against the deployment, not code the package ships -->\n```js\ndb.hal_sessions.updateMany({entryCount: {$exists: false}}, [{$set: {entryCount: {$size: '$entries'}}}]);\n```\n\n`InMemorySessionStore` goes by a session's newest entry, or its creation for a session with none,\nand never lists one that has aged out. One divergence to know about, in that store only: where two\nof a user's conversations are last active in the same millisecond, the list puts the larger session\nid first while `latestFor` takes the one created later, so for tied conversations the head of the\nlist and the session a resume rejoins can differ. `MongoSessionStore` breaks that tie the same way\nin both members, so the two agree there.\n\nA store you write yourself can leave `listFor` out, in which case it has no conversation list to\noffer. One built on an injected collection needs that collection to implement `find`: without it,\n`listFor` refuses rather than reporting that the user has no conversations.\n\n**GDPR.** A summary is personal data: it shows that a user held a conversation, and when. It\ncarries no message content, and the user's id is part of the query rather than a filter applied\nafterwards, so a list can only ever be one user's. How far back the list reaches is the retention\ndecision, and it is yours — see § Retention.\n\n## Lookup\n\n`lookup(sessionId)` is optional. It answers one of three things: `{status: 'active', session}`,\n`{status: 'expired', userId}`, which carries the owner's id so ownership can be checked and never\nthe conversation, or `{status: 'missing'}`. `missing` is always a permitted answer, and leaving\n`lookup` out behaves exactly as before: resume reads `get`, and a failed resume reads `unknown`.\n\n`lookup` reports a lifetime decision rather than making one: `maxAgeMs` is a memory bound, not a\nretention period, and a tombstone index of ids a store no longer holds is rejected, so an expired\nsession is reported once and then forgotten. `InMemorySessionStore` implements it that way.\n`MongoSessionStore` does not implement it: its documents do not expire, and one that\n`eraseOlderThan` removed reads `unknown`.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":145,"oldLines":8,"newStart":145,"newLines":9,"lines":[" in both members, so the two agree there."," "," A store you write yourself can leave `listFor` out, in which case it has no conversation list to","-offer. One built on an injected collection needs that collection to implement `find`: without it,","-`listFor` refuses rather than reporting that the user has no conversations.","+offer, and a client's `list_sessions` frame is answered with an `error` frame (`UNSUPPORTED`) rather","+than an empty list. One built on an injected collection needs that collection to implement `find`:","+without it, `listFor` refuses rather than reporting that the user has no conversations."," "," **GDPR.** A summary is personal data: it shows that a user held a conversation, and when. It"," carries no message content, and the user's id is part of the query rather than a filter applied"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_9b79feeddf4142c18f910354","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

The acceptance test's expectation for this one case was corrected to the error frame and the handler, protocol spec § 5.6/§ 5.9, conversation-list spec, CHANGELOG and docs/session-stores.md all state it (`src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts` › answers a store without listFor with UNSUPPORTED rather than an empty list).","originalFile":"# Definition of Done\n\n> #143 gives a consumer `store.listFor(userId)` inside the server process. The client on the other end of the WebSocket has no way to ask for it, and the consumer who wants a conversation picker without standing up their own REST endpoint has to write one anyway.\n\n**Strategy: `direct`** — `createServer` and the WebSocket upgrade/message pipeline already exist and accept frames over a real WebSocket connection, so acceptance tests can connect today, send `list_sessions` frames, and fail directly on the missing `session_list` and `list_sessions` validation/dispatch behaviour.\n\n## Done when these pass\n\n- [ ] **listing conversations over the WebSocket protocol › answers list_sessions for the authenticated user with ISO dates, forwarding limit and before while ignoring any client userId** — Sends `{type: 'list_sessions', limit, before, userId}` over a connected WebSocket and verifies `store.listFor` is called with the socket's authenticated `userId` (`session.userId`) and `{limit, before}`, answering `{type: 'session_list', sessions}` with `createdAt` and `updatedAt` serialised as ISO-8601 strings.\n  `src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts`\n\n- [ ] **listing conversations over the WebSocket protocol › answers an empty session_list when the store has no listFor, and SERVER_ERROR with a ws error log when listFor throws** — Verifies that a store without `listFor` answers `{type: 'session_list', sessions: []}` and a store whose `listFor` throws/rejects logs an error under category `'ws'` with the userId and error message and answers `{type: 'error', code: 'SERVER_ERROR'}`.\n  `src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts`\n\n- [ ] **listing conversations over the WebSocket protocol › accepts a bare list_sessions frame and rejects a malformed limit or before with INVALID_MESSAGE without calling listFor** — Verifies that `{type: 'list_sessions'}` is accepted while non-integer or negative `limit` values and malformed `before` cursors (`sessionId` outside 1–128 chars or unparseable `updatedAt`) are rejected with `INVALID_MESSAGE` without invoking `store.listFor`.\n  `src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts`\n\n## Facets\n\n- [x] Add `ListSessionsMessage`, `SessionSummaryFrame`, and `SessionListMessage` to `src/types/messages.ts`, include them in `IncomingMessage` and `OutgoingMessage`, and re-export them from `src/index.ts`.\n- [x] Validate `list_sessions` frames in `src/transport/ws/validation.ts` (optional non-negative integer `limit`; optional `before` object with 1–128 char `sessionId` and finite-date `updatedAt` string or number; strip unknown fields like `userId`).\n- [x] Thread `sessionStore` into `createMessageHandler` (optional parameter so existing 1-arg and 2-arg callers keep working) and wire it in `src/transport/createServer.ts`.\n- [x] Handle `list_sessions` in `src/transport/ws/messageHandler.ts` (and helper in `src/transport/ws/sender.ts` if needed) by reading `session.userId`, calling `await sessionStore?.listFor?.(session.userId, {limit, before})`, serialising `Date` fields to ISO strings, and on error logging via `log.error('ws', ...)` and sending `ErrorCodes.SERVER_ERROR`.\n- [x] Pin the off-the-lock answering with a regression test: a `list_sessions` sent while a `user_message` run is pending is answered before that turn's `stream_end` (`src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts` › one message at a time per session).\n- [x] Document `list_sessions` and `session_list` in `specs/hal-engine-websocket-protocol/spec.md` (§ 4.3, § 5.9: field tables, authorisation rule, off-the-lock rule) and `specs/hal-engine-conversation-list/spec.md` § Over the WebSocket protocol (with the trailing `([validated by ...])` citations for the acceptance tests and `src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts` › a conversation list, then set the conversation-list spec's transport statements' Status).\n- [ ] Decide the answer to a store that implements no `listFor`: the ticket text says an `error` frame, never an empty list (\"an empty history is not a safe guess\"), while this branch's acceptance test, handler and CHANGELOG pin an empty `session_list`. The two disagree; changing either is a behaviour decision to make explicitly, not a mechanical fix.\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Conversation titles or previews (first user message, model-generated title).\n- Deleting or renaming a conversation from the client over the socket.\n- Switching the socket's active session in place (`?sessionId=` on reconnect is how a conversation is rejoined).\n- Holding pagination cursor state server-side (the client pages with `before`).\n- An operator view of another user's conversations or live sync between open tabs.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":23,"oldLines":7,"newStart":23,"newLines":7,"lines":[" - [x] Handle `list_sessions` in `src/transport/ws/messageHandler.ts` (and helper in `src/transport/ws/sender.ts` if needed) by reading `session.userId`, calling `await sessionStore?.listFor?.(session.userId, {limit, before})`, serialising `Date` fields to ISO strings, and on error logging via `log.error('ws', ...)` and sending `ErrorCodes.SERVER_ERROR`."," - [x] Pin the off-the-lock answering with a regression test: a `list_sessions` sent while a `user_message` run is pending is answered before that turn's `stream_end` (`src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts` › one message at a time per session)."," - [x] Document `list_sessions` and `session_list` in `specs/hal-engine-websocket-protocol/spec.md` (§ 4.3, § 5.9: field tables, authorisation rule, off-the-lock rule) and `specs/hal-engine-conversation-list/spec.md` § Over the WebSocket protocol (with the trailing `([validated by ...])` citations for the acceptance tests and `src/transport/ws/messageHandler.test.ts` › a conversation list, then set the conversation-list spec's transport statements' Status).","-- [ ] Decide the answer to a store that implements no `listFor`: the ticket text says an `error` frame, never an empty list (\"an empty history is not a safe guess\"), while this branch's acceptance test, handler and CHANGELOG pin an empty `session_list`.
